title: CounterScene: Counterfactual Causal Reasoning in Generative World Models for Safety-Critical Closed-Loop Evaluation

control_signal.value: Automatically identified causally critical adversarial agent and conflict point; guidance targets removing that agent's spatial and temporal safety margins relative to the ego. No user-facing control knob described.

control_mechanism.value: Gradients of a spatial, temporal and jerk guidance loss during diffusion denoising modify only the adversarial agent's trajectory; the world model, with a causal interaction graph, handles other agents' responses.

base_model.value: Conditional diffusion BEV world model with SceneTransformer denoiser, augmented with a learned Causal Interaction Graph; 100 diffusion steps.

datasets.value: Trained on nuScenes train split, evaluated on 100 nuScenes validation scenes via tbsim; zero-shot transfer to a curated 100-scene nuPlan set.

metrics.value: Realism: ADE, FDE, off-road rate (ORR). Adversarial effectiveness: collision rate (CR) and hard braking rate (HBR).

controllability_evidence.value: At 8-10 s horizon, CR is 22.7% versus 12.3% for CCDiff, with lower ADE (1.877 vs 2.092). An ablation variant with ADE 0.798 reports CR 6.5%; the packet does not say this is the 8-10 s setting.

stated_limitations.value: No explicit limitations in packet; future work says the framework intervenes on a single causally critical agent and calls for a unified scene-agent formulation.

notes: Control here is adversarial intensity via automatic guidance, not user-specified attributes. Best of 16 rollouts is selected per scene for all methods.
